[[Category:Artificial neural network]]
'''Layer normalisation''' (LN) normalises an input matrix $\mathbf{X}$ row-wise so each row $\vec x_i=(x_j)$ satisfies:

$$
\overline x_j = 0\\
\sigma_{x_j} = 1
$$

== Definition ==

i.e., if

$$
(\mathbf{X})_{i,}=\vec x_i = (x_j)
$$

then

$$
(\operatorname{LN}(\mathbf{X}))_{i,}
=\vec\gamma\odot\frac{\vec x_i-\overline x_j \dots \vec 1}{\sqrt{\sigma^{2}+\epsilon}}+\vec\beta,
\qquad
\overline x_j=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{j=1}^{d}x_j,
\qquad
\sigma^{2}=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{j=1}^{d}\left(x_j-\overline x_j\right)^{2},
$$

where $\vec\gamma,\vec\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ are learnt [[model parameters (ANN)|model parameters]], known as the '''gain''' and '''bias''' of layer normalisation, and $\odot$ denotes the [[Hadamard-Schur product]].
